evidence.quote: I anticipate that further gradual increases in the policy rate will be appropriate to both sustain a healthy labor market and stabilize inflation around our 2 percent objective.
In my view, the economy appears to be in a good spot right now. This favorable position is particularly evident in the labor market.
I tend to agree with the view that the recent softness of inflation mostly reflects idiosyncratic and transitory factors, and I expect inflation to move back to 2 percent over the next year or so.
I think it is worthwhile to acknowledge that there are some upside risks to the forecast and to think through what the consequences of those risks materializing might be.
As the natural rate moves up, any given level of the policy rate would be more accommodative, so the policy rate would also have to move up to continue the gradual removal of policy accommodation.

parsed.rationale: The speaker is optimistic on growth and labor, views low inflation as transitory, flags upside growth risks and a possibly higher natural rate, and endorses further gradual rate increases. Caveats about supply-led growth damping inflation keep this at a moderate hawkish lean.
